svg.text: Simple, open, and suspicious of input
The second half of the design group: assume the input is hostile and the compromise is coming.

g.text: P9 · ECONOMY OF MECHANISM — simplicity is a security control
Server-rendered HTML, no SPA, one database — a stack small enough that one team can actually audit it.
P10 · OPEN DESIGN — security never depends on secrecy of design
Architecture, lifecycle and this principle set are documented and shipped; only credentials are secret.
P11 · DON'T TRUST INPUT — from users, integrations, or the LLM
Allowlists over sanitisers, autoescaped templates, strict CSP with zero inline styles or handlers — enforced, not aspired to.
P12 · MAKE COMPROMISE DETECTION EASIER — assume you'll need the trail
Audit logs, canaries, and a tamper-evident sha256 evidence ledger — the platform expects to be investigated.
P13 · REDUCE IMPACT OF COMPROMISE — contain, minimise, expire
Data-minimisation audited schema-wide; scoped tokens that hard-expire; container isolation per service.
